answer: Give every agent a quartz-hard identity key that must continuously advance its own verifiable-delay chain, like a plume of smoke that only rises at one fixed speed: each step output seeds the next, so no farm can run one chain for many identities, split one chain across machines, or buy its way ahead, because extra hardware cannot shorten sequential time. Each fake identity therefore costs a full dedicated sequential run lasting the whole qualification window, while a zephyr of cheap parallel machines gains nothing, because time, not throughput, is the price of being counted as one.
